To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in patients with melanoma and multiple positive sentinel lymph node biopsy, complete lymph node dissections do not result in improved progression‐free survival or melanoma‐specific overall survival.
patients with multiple positive nodes had a significantly higher risk of non‐SLN metastasis.
patients with multiple positive lymph nodes have a worse survival compared with patients with one positive lymph node and that CLND did not improve survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of sentinel node biopsy in patients with multiple metastatic sentinel nodes.
the analysis of lymph node dissection in patients with multiple sentinel lymph nodes.
the question whether the complete lymph node dissections (CLND) of melanoma patients with more than 1 positive sentinel lymph node improves the prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CLND in patients with multiple SLNs does not improve survival and therefore is not indicated.
CLND should only be performed in patients with multiple SLN metastases in whom the risk of non‐SLN metastases is high.
CLND in patients with multiple SLN is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of SLN metastases does not predict the number of positive non‐SLNs and therefore the necessity of CLND.
CLND in patients with multiple SLN did not improve MSS and PFS.
the presence of multiple positive SLN in itself is not an indication for CLND.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of multiple positive SLN is a strong predictor of nodal metastasis, but does not significantly improve survival.
patients with multiple positive nodes are not necessarily candidates for CLND.
the presence of multiple positive SLN is a prognostic marker for the development of distant metastases.
